instructions: For Whipped Ricotta & Toppings:
For the Whipped Ricotta
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Slice the baguette into 1-inch slices. Arrange the bread slices on a rack placed in a large rimmed baking sheet. - 1 baguette

Brush the slices with olive oil, season to taste with salt and pepper, then bake for 6-8 minutes per side or until crisp and lightly browned. Reserve until ready to serve. - 1 baguette - olive oil as needed - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste
Add the ricotta and lemon zest to the bowl of a food processor. While the machine is running, stream in the olive oil. - 8 oz whole milk ricotta - ½ lemon zested - 1 ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then serve with Topping(s) of choice (see recipes below) and baguette slices. - freshly ground black pepper to taste - kosher salt to taste
For the Confit Tomatoes
Preheat the oven to 275 °F.
Combine the tomatoes, garlic, basil, and bay leaf in a small ceramic baking dish. - 8 oz cherry tomatoes - 3 garlic cloves smashed - 4 ½ basil leaves - 1 bay leaf

Pour the olive oil over the ingredients until the tomatoes are mostly covered and season generously with salt, pepper, and chiles (if using). - 1 ½ cup mild olive oil - kosher salt to taste - ½ tsp black peppercorns - 2 Chiles de arbol optional
Bake for 1 ½ - 2 hours covered. - For the Confit Tomatoes
Serve the tomatoes over Whipped Ricotta and finish with a drizzle of the confit oil and more salt. - For the Confit Tomatoes - 8 oz Whipped Ricotta (see recipe above) - kosher salt to taste
For the Basil Oil
Blanch the basil leaves in boiling water for 15 seconds. Then, transfer the basil leaves to an ice bath to cool. - 1 cup basil leaves packed

Strain the basil leaves and place them in the bowl of a food processor. Add the oil and salt, then process until the mixture is pureed. - 1 cup basil leaves packed - ½ cup extra virgin olive oil - pinch kosher salt
Allow the mixture to sit in the refrigerator for 1 hour or up to 8 hours. - For the Basil Oil
Bring the oil back to room temperature, then strain and use. - For the Basil Oil
For the Deconstructed Pesto
Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
Add the pinenuts to a small skillet. - ⅓ cup pinenuts
Toast the nuts over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, or until fragrant and lightly browned. Remove them from the pan and allow them to cool. - ⅓ cup pinenuts
Add the garlic cloves to the Whipped Ricotta and stir to combine. - 1 garlic clove minced or crushed - 8 oz Whipped Ricotta (see recipe above)

Sprinkle the pinenuts over the Whipped Ricotta mixture and drizzle with Basil Oil. Top with the parmesan cheese, basil leaves, and season with flaky salt. - ⅓ cup pinenuts - 1 garlic clove minced or crushed - 8 oz Whipped Ricotta (see recipe above) - 2 ½ tbsp Basil Oil (see recipe above) - ¼ cup parmesan cheese grated - 2 ½ basil leaves - flaky salt to taste
For the Browned Butter Sage
Toast the pistachios in a small pan for 4-5 minutes or until fragrant and lightly browned. Reserve until ready to serve.

Melt the butter over medium-low heat in a skillet. Add the sage and continue cooking the butter until the butter solids have browned, about 4-5 minutes. Make sure to stir or swirl the mixture periodically to avoid burning.
Drizzle the browned butter over the Whipped Ricotta, top with a drizzle of honey, reserved pistachios, salt, and pepper.
For Cornish Hen & Sauces:
For the Cornish Hen
Split the cornish hens in half lengthwise using a sharp cleaver or poultry shears. - 2 Cornish hens

Combine the salt, pepper, and baking powder in a small bowl. Generously coat the hens in the dry brine. - ½ cup kosher salt plus more to taste - 2 tsp freshly ground black pepper plus more to taste - 1 tsp baking powder - 2 Cornish hens
Refrigerate the hens, uncovered, on a rimmed baking sheet for a minimum of 4 hours or up to 24 hours. - 2 Cornish hens
Preheat the oven to 450 °F.

Pat the hens dry and brush the hens down with melted duck fat, then season generously with salt and pepper. - 2 Cornish hens - ¼ cup duck fat melted (or clarified butter) - ½ cup kosher salt plus more to taste - 2 tsp freshly ground black pepper plus more to taste

Place the chopped vegetables, herbs, and garlic in a large rimmed baking sheet. - 2 yellow onions roughly chopped - 4 celery stalks roughly chopped - 3 large carrots roughly chopped - 2 sprigs rosemary - 4 ½ thyme sprigs - 6 garlic cloves smashed
Place a rack over the vegetables and transfer the cornish hens to the racks, skin-side up. - 2 Cornish hens

Roast the hens for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown. Reduce the heat to 375 °F, then roast for an additional 35-40 minutes or until the internal temperature of the thickest part of the thigh reaches 180 °F and the breast reaches 170 °F. - For the Cornish Hen
Strain and reserve the pan drippings. Allow the birds to rest for 10-15 minutes before serving. - For the Cornish Hen

Alternatively, after patting the dry-brined chickens dry, transfer them to a cold high-sided skillet, skin-side down. Cook the hens over medium-high heat until the skin has browned, about 6-8 minutes. Flip the hens over and transfer them to a 375 °F oven. Then roast for an additional 35-40 minutes or until the internal temperature of the thickest part of the thigh reaches 180 °F and the breast reaches 170 °F. Reserve the pan with the fond for the pan sauce (see recipe below). - For the Cornish Hen
Serve with parsnip puree (see recipe below) and sauce of choice. - For the Cornish Hen - For the Parsnip Puree
For the Simple Mustard Pan Sauce
Over medium heat, re-heat the reserved drippings or fond in the skillet. Add the shallot and cook for 3-4 minutes or until tender. - 2 tbsp reserved drippings or fond - ½ shallot minced
Deglaze the pan with chicken stock. Add the lemon juice and simmer the sauce until it has reduced by about 75%. - 1 cup chicken stock preferably homemade - ½ lemon juiced
Once reduced, turn off the heat and add the mustard and butter. Whisk to combine the sauce. - 1 tsp Dijon mustard - 3 tbsp unsalted butter
Season the sauce to taste with salt and pepper, then garnish with parsley. - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste - ¼ cup parsley chopped, to garnish
For the Gremolata

Combine the parsley, shallot, garlic, lemon zest, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. - ¾ cup parsley chopped - ½ shallot minced - 1 garlic clove minced - 1 lemon zested - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste
Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve. - For the Gremolata
For the Fig Port Sauce
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet. Add the shallot and cook until just turning translucent, about 2-3 minutes. - 1 tbsp olive oil - 1 shallot finely chopped

Add the port and chicken stock, rosemary, and figs to the skillet. Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until the sauce has reduced by 75%. - 1 cup port - ¾ cup chicken stock preferably homemade - 1 sprig rosemary - 8 fresh mission figs quartered
Turn off the heat and mount the sauce with the cold butter. - 2 tbsp unsalted butter cubed and cold
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then serve immediately. - kosher salt. to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste
For the Parsnip Puree

Add the parsnips, milk, cream, garlic, thyme, and a pinch of salt to a medium pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then continue cooking for 12-15 minutes or until the parsnips are completely tender. - 1 lb parsnips peeled and cut into one inch pieces - ¾ cup whole milk - ¾ cup heavy cream - 3 ½ cloves garlic roasted or confit - 2 sprigs thyme

Using a slotted spoon, transfer the parsnips and butter to a food processor. With the machine running, stream in enough milk/cream mixture to form a smooth puree. - 1 lb parsnips peeled and cut into one inch pieces - 2 tbsp unsalted butter
Season the parsnip puree to taste with salt and white pepper. - For the Parsnip Puree - kosher salt to taste - white pepper to taste
For Crème brûlée:
For the Superfine Sugar
Blend the sugar in a food processor for 3-4 minutes. - ½ cup sugar
Reserve until ready to use.
For the Vanilla Crème brûlée
Preheat the oven to 275 °F with convection. Place a cake pan filled with about 2 inches of water in the oven to preheat.

Combine the heavy cream, about ½ the sugar, salt, and vanilla bean (seeds and pod) in a small pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then turn off the heat. Let the mixture sit while the next step is prepared. - 10 oz heavy cream - 2 oz granulated sugar divided - ¼ tsp kosher salt - 1 vanilla bean pod seeds removed and reserved
In a medium bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and the remaining sugar. - 3 large egg yolks - 2 oz granulated sugar divided
Temper the hot cream mixture into the egg yolk mixture. - 10 oz heavy cream - 3 large egg yolks
Strain the creme brulee batter and deposit it into two 6-oz ramekins. Remove any bubbles from the surface using a torch. - For the Vanilla Crème brûlée
Transfer the filled ramekins to the preheated water bath in the oven. - For the Vanilla Crème brûlée
Bake the creme brulees for 20-25 minutes or until just the center remains wobbly. - For the Vanilla Crème brûlée
Let the creme brulees cool inside the water bath until they reach room temperature, about 2 hours. - For the Vanilla Crème brûlée
Wrap and transfer the creme brulees to the refrigerator to chill overnight. - For the Vanilla Crème brûlée

When ready to serve, sprinkle a thin layer of super fine sugar over the surface of each creme brulee. Torch the sugar until caramelized. - For the Vanilla Crème brûlée - Superfine sugar as needed (see recipe above)
For the Matcha Crème brûlée
Preheat the oven to 275 °F with convection. Place a cake pan filled with about 2 inches of water in the oven to preheat.
Whisk together about ½ the sugar and matcha together. - 2 oz granulated sugar divided - 1 ½ tsp matcha powder

Combine the heavy cream, sugar/matcha mixture, and salt in a small pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then turn off the heat. Let the mixture sit while the next step is prepared. - 10 oz heavy cream - 2 oz granulated sugar divided - 1 ½ tsp matcha powder - ¼ tsp kosher salt
In a medium bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and the remaining sugar. - 3 large egg yolks - 2 oz granulated sugar divided
Temper the hot cream mixture into the egg yolk mixture. - 10 oz heavy cream - 3 large egg yolks
Strain the creme brulee batter and deposit it into two 6-oz ramekins. Remove any bubbles from the surface using a torch. - For the Matcha Crème brûlée
Transfer the filled ramekins to the preheated water bath in the oven.
Bake the creme brulees for 20-25 minutes or until just the center remains wobbly. - For the Matcha Crème brûlée
Let the creme brulees cool inside the water bath until they reach room temperature, about 2 hours. - For the Matcha Crème brûlée
Wrap and transfer the creme brulees to the refrigerator to chill overnight. - For the Matcha Crème brûlée

When ready to serve, sprinkle a thin layer of super fine sugar over the surface of each creme brulee. Torch the sugar until caramelized. - For the Matcha Crème brûlée - Superfine sugar as needed (see recipe above)
For the Citrus Crème brûlée
Combine the heavy cream and orange zest in a small bowl. Refrigerate for 2 hours to allow the heavy cream to infuse. - 10 oz heavy cream - 3 oranges zested
Preheat the oven to 275 °F with convection. Place a cake pan filled with about 2 inches of water in the oven to preheat.

Combine the steeped heavy cream, about ½ the sugar, and salt in a small pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then turn off the heat. Let the mixture sit while the next step is prepared. - 10 oz heavy cream - 2 oz granulated sugar divided - ¼ tsp kosher salt
In a medium bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, lemon juice, and the remaining sugar. - 3 large egg yolks - 1 ½ tbsp lemon juice preferably meyer lemons - 2 oz granulated sugar divided
Temper the hot cream mixture into the egg yolk mixture. - 10 oz heavy cream - 3 large egg yolks
Strain the creme brulee batter and deposit it into two 6-oz ramekins. Remove any bubbles from the surface using a torch. - For the Citrus Crème brûlée
Transfer the filled ramekins to the preheated water bath in the oven.
Bake the creme brulees for 20-25 minutes or until just the center remains wobbly. - For the Citrus Crème brûlée
Let the creme brulees cool inside the water bath until they reach room temperature, about 2 hours. - For the Citrus Crème brûlée
Wrap and transfer the creme brulees to the refrigerator to chill overnight. - For the Citrus Crème brûlée

When ready to serve, sprinkle a thin layer of superfine sugar over the surface of each creme brulee. Torch the sugar until caramelized. - For the Citrus Crème brûlée - Superfine sugar as needed (see recipe above)
